newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank robbery "mole" jailed for 14 years.
newsitem.headline: French bank robbery "mole" jailed for 14 years.

text.p: A bank secretary was sentenced to 14 years in jail for passing information to robbers who made off with 146 million francs ($29 million) two years ago, justice sources said on Saturday.

Helene Renaux, 40, described by work colleagues as the perfect secretary, was accused of providing her lover, Jean-Claude Lopiccolo, with information on security at a branch of the Bank of France in the Mediterranean port of Toulon.
The robbers kidnapped a bank employee from his home and, after strapping remote-controlled explosives around his chest, forced him to open the doors of the bank.
The assize court in the southern town of Draguignan also jailed the group's two leaders, Dominique Bernarini and Marc Armando, for 18 years.
Lopiccolo got 14 years and five other accomplices received sentences ranging from three to 10 years.
Only one-tenth of the stolen money was ever recovered, and police say several accomplices are still on the run.
